newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN UNIWEAR IN MACKIE SHARE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN UNIWEAR IN MACKIE SHARE DEAL.

text.p: Belgian textiles holding company Uniwear SA said on Friday it aimed to place 150,000 Uniwear shares held by its minority shareholder Mackie International Group Plc with its main shareholder Connie Inc.
The placement is part of a capital increase by Mackie to re-pay debtors. Before the deal Mackie, a Northern Irish textiles machines maker, held 9.6 percent of Uniwear.
Uniwear did not say in its statement what Mackie's stake would be after the transaction.
Mackie lost 7.2 million sterling before taxes in 1996 on turnover of 12.6 million. It said earlier this week it planned a five-for-two rights issue to raise 5.25 million sterling.

Uniwear said it would commit to buying back the shares provided its general assembly of shareholders approved such a buy-back. According to its articles of association the company cannot buy back more than 10 percent of the shares issued.
Uniwear said it would continue a restricted cooperation with Mackie involving testing a new machine and commercial cooperation in China.
